title: Epigenome Editing in Opioid Action
text:
We propose to develop a cell type specific and temporal specific epigenome editing tool that will have the
capability of altering epigenetic marks or transcription marks on opioid disrupted gene loci in specific neuron
subtypes. We will test these tools in specific neuron subtypes in the brain in opioid mediate gene expression
networks and behaviors.

title: Decoding the mechanism of inflammatory memory in human epithelia
text:
Remitting-relapsing inflammatory disorders affect millions of people and have no cure despite periods of
treatment success. Inflammation lastingly alters long-lived epithelial cells in psoriasis and may predispose them
to relapse and epidermal pathology. We propose to decode the mechanism that underlies this inflammatory
memory in human epithelial cells.

title: Identification of AAV capsids with superior skeletal muscle transduction capability using cross-species analysis model
text:
A broad range of muscular dystrophies are caused by inherited genetic variants. Gene therapy is a
promising means of supporting life-long treatment by reconstituting expression of functional gene products.
Recent gene therapy failures highlight the need for improved vector targeting and mitigated immunological
responses, however. Ventura Life Sciences was founded to apply state-of-the-art directed evolution strategies to
the development of novel AAV capsids with key features driving improved safety and efficacy.

title: Single-Scan Multi-Contrast Cranial MRI in Pediatric Patients
text:
Children with congenital abnormalities of the skull typically require surgery, which is aided by three-dimensional
images of the skull obtained by X-ray computed tomography (CT) guiding the surgeon. While CT is the current
modality of choice, repeated scanning puts pediatric patients at risk of adverse health outcomes later in life. The
proposed work, building on preliminary studies demonstrating feasibility, is based on magnetic resonance
imaging (MRI), which is projected to yield images similar in quality to CT while being free of harmful radiation.

title: Personalized genomics signal deconvolution to improve cell-type level inference
text:
Clinical bulk samples contain mixed cell types, resulting to an admixture of signals from multiple pure compo-
nents. We propose to develop novel statistical approaches to address the problem of cell type mixture identifi-
cation for subjects with multiple observations, construct methods to estimate individual-specific pure profile ref-
erences, and retrieve more accurate cell type mixture proportions at individual levels. Our project will break new
ground for many studies by enabling the investigation of personalized pure cell type associations with the disease
outcome, and the individual-level, cell-type-specific biomarker discovery.

title: Protein Carbonylation as a Mechanistic Driver and Biomarker of Sarcopenia
text:
Lipid carbonyls are reactive electrophilic metabolites that accumulate with age and induce cell damage via
modification of proteins. Scavenging carbonyls by treating mice with N-acetyl-carnosine prevents muscle
weakness in old mice. This project will use a novel mass spectrometry method to comprehensively
characterize the carbonyl proteomes in muscle tissues from aging mice and plasma from humans across a
broad age-range to uncover the key protein modifications that may be driving muscle weakness and atrophy.

title: Automated Platform for Critical Quality Analytics in Cell Therapy Manufacturing
text:
Cell therapy manufacturing currently operates with episodic, offline quality control (QC), resulting in delayed
process feedback, elevated batch failure rates, and limited scalability–factors that constrain patient access to
life-saving treatments. This project advances an automated platform that embeds QC into the manufacturing
workflow, continuously monitoring critical control parameters in real time, without human intervention. By
enabling early detection of deviations, improving product uniformity, and eliminating reliance on manual assays,
the technology will unlock scalability, lower manufacturing costs, and accelerate the delivery of high-quality
therapeutic cells. In doing so, it expands the reach of curative immunotherapies, making them more reliable,
affordable, and broadly available to patients worldwide.

title: Neural regulation of susceptibility to hyperarousal
text:
Exposure to traumatic stress, as is common during combat, can lead to post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
in susceptible individuals. As such, the lifetime prevalence of PTSD in combat soldiers is 6-30%. In addition to
the debilitating consequences on mental health, PTSD is associated with an increased risk of developing
cardiovascular disease. Abnormal increases in the fight-or-flight neurotransmitter, norepinephrine, are thought
to contribute to the development of hyperarousal, a major symptom of PTSD and facilitator of cardiovascular
disease. The overarching goal of our research is to use an animal model of combat-related trauma to identify
druggable targets that can improve regulation of hyperarousal. Specifically, these studies will test the hypothesis
that an inflammatory molecule signaling within the locus coeruleus, a stress-sensitive brain region, promotes
trauma-induced behavioral and cardiovascular risk in males and females.

title: Causal mechanisms driving germline predisposition to myeloproliferative disorders
text:
While risk for chronic blood disorders such as myeloproliferative neoplasms vary depending on one’s genetic
background, the basis of this variation is unknown. The overall goal of this project is to understand the
mechanisms by which some individuals may be predisposed to myeloproliferative neoplasms, as a result of their
genetic makeup. We will study this by testing how inherited genetic variants expand mutant clones of blood
forming stem cells to cause this disease.

title: Utility of human milk oligosaccharides against the perinatal pathogen, Group B Streptococcus
text:
Streptococcus agalactiae is a Gram positive bacterium that can cause invasive infections during pregnancy
which lead to severe disease outcomes including premature rupture of gestational membranes, preterm birth,
neonatal sepsis and death. This translational research project seeks to determine if application of human breast
milk sugars can prevent S. agalactiae pathogenesis, the host immune response and disease progression. The
results from the proposed experiments could lead to new approaches for the prevention of GBS-associated
diseases and cost-effective treatment strategies to mitigate the risk of infections during pregnancy.

title: Lipidomics Shared Resource Core
text:
This Core serves as an analytical platform for the study of a large family of lipids (sphingolipids) and their 
metabolizing enzymes. Using targeted mass spectrometry, the Core provides unique, well-established, and 
consolidated methods to measure the more than 300 individual different species of sphingolipids, home- 
developed methods to monitor the in vitro and in situ enzymatic activities of the enzymes involved in the 
metabolism of these lipids and MALDI imaging on tissue samples.

title: Oscillatory Neural Correlates of Motor Phenotypes in Parkinson Disease
text:
Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of subthalamic nucleus (STN) and globus pallidus internus (GPi) has largely
replaced ablative techniques in the surgical treatment of Parkinson Disease (PD) but very limited data exists
regarding the electrophysiological abnormalities within these structures for subtypes of PD. In this project, we
show initial evidence of electrophysiological footprints of PD motor phenotypes within the territories of STN.
Based on these key preliminary observations, we propose to investigate dynamics of oscillatory neural activity
recorded from the territories of STN and GPi with high resolution electrodes during wake DBS surgery for the
personalization and optimization of DBS in PD.

title: Impacts of Staphylococcus aureus nitric oxide synthase on survival and physiological modulation in host environments
text:
Staphylococcus aureus is a highly adaptable pathogen that can infect nearly all human tissue and organ systems,
due in large part to its versatile metabolism. S. aureus nitric oxide (NO) production through its NO synthase
enzyme impacts its ability to modulate cellular metabolism, stress resistance and virulence. The studies
proposed in this application will facilitate a mechanistic understanding of how bacterial endogenous NO
production modulates physiology within and/or between bacterial cells and its specific impact on host biology
and virulence, and as such, may uncover novel therapeutic targets or treatment strategies against S. aureus and
other pathogens that produce NO.

title: Investigating Molecular Mechanisms of Alternating Hemiplegia of Childhood Using C. elegans Models
text:
Mutations in ATP1A3, a Na+, K+ ATPase, cause Alternating Hemiplegia of Childhood (AHC) through an
unknown mechanism. In this proposal, I use C. elegans as a model organism to investigate properties of the
Na+, K+ ATPase and determine how AHC patient mutations impair normal function. Completion of this project
will provide foundational information for future studies that delineate the cellular mechanisms perturbed in AHC
and investigate targets for therapy development.

title: Transcriptional Regulation of the Microbiota-Nutrition Axis in Genetically Diverse Macrophages During Psoriasiform Inflammation.
text:
Project Narra+ve
 Psoriasis is a chronic, systemic inflammatory disease driven by complex interactions
between polygenic host susceptibilities and environmental triggers like diet and the microbiome,
with contributions from immune cells such as macrophages. In this project, I will use genetically
diverse mice and employ single-cell multi-omics approaches to explore the transcriptional,
epigenetic, and proteomic landscape during psoriasiform inflammation influenced by diet and
the skin microbiome. Beyond advancing novel analysis methods that integrate multi-omics with
genetic and microbiome data, this research aims to enhance our understanding of psoriasis
etiology and uncover therapeutic targets by elucidating how genetic diversity shapes the
nutrition-microbiome-immune axis.

title: Center for Team Effectiveness to Accelerate EBP Implementation in Children's Mental Health Services: Methods Core
text: (Methods Core) Team approaches to meet organizational goals are utilized broadly and globally in industry, the military, space exploration, and health settings. The TEAMS Methods Core is integral to adapting and advancing team-based models, approaches, strategies, methods, and evaluation for children’s mental health and for the larger center activities. Of note, the Methods Core will lead innovation by leveraging natural language processing (NLP) technology to develop tools to rapidly assess team functioning in real-world settings. Within community service systems caring for children with mental health needs, the assessment of team effectiveness—although crucial for improving team functioning—can be a laborious and cumbersome task. Innovations in technology related to the automatic capturing of communication between team members can lessen the burden in assessing and improving team effectiveness. The Methods Core will lead innovation by leveraging natural language processing technology to develop tools to rapidly assess team functioning in real-world settings. The Methods Core investigators have already been collaborating closely with the Administrative Core, the R01, and the R34 teams, and Community Service System Workgroup stakeholders in selecting, adapting and shaping strategies and approaches to implementation and improvement for children’s mental health across service system settings. The Methods Core is a team effort led by Drs. Aarons (implementation science, mental health), Burke (team effectiveness, team strategies), and Sklar (mental health services, evaluation) (see biosketches). The Methods Core is organized to address four aims: Aim 1) Integrate models and strategies from team effectiveness research and implementation science to improve children’s mental health services, Aim 2) Apply multilevel and advanced methods and designs for team-based implementation research, and Aim 3) Lead the design and implementation of a multi-level, longitudinal, iterative evaluation to refine the Center’s research activities, maximize the Center’s impact and inform plans for future collaborative research.

title: AI-empowered 3D Computer Vision and Image-Omics Integration for Digital Kidney Histopathology
text:
Computer-assisted interpretation of renal histopathology using whole slide imaging (WSI) has dramatically
advanced both the research and practice for the diagnosis and scoring of specific causes of chronic kidney
disease (CKD). However, current phenotyping approaches are restricted to investigating two dimensional (2D)
sections, which are error-prone due to the heterogeneity of kidney tissue (e.g., glomeruli) across three
dimensional (3D) serial sectioning. We seek to enable AI-empowered 3D interpretation of routine digital renal
histopathology, so as to (1) allow renal pathologists to perform a reproducible 3D phenotyping on serial 2D whole
slide images (WSI), (2) advance the characterization of kidney-allograft rejection phenotypes on kidney
transplant patients with cutting-edge 3D computer vision, and (3) equip clinical scientists with an advanced 3D
spatial transcriptomics analytics tool to investigate the anatomical-molecular associated causes of chronic kidney
disease (CKD).

title: PDX Core
text: PDX CORE PROJECT SUMMARY The goals of the PDTC PDX Core are to establish and maintain PDX lines for the purpose of conducting animal preclinical trials using experimental and standard-of-care therapeutics; to promote quality control, reproducibility, and collaboration by developing and maintaining shared Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for PDX development, maintenance, experimentation, and pathogen testing; to provide infrastructure to manage large PDX collections and to generate, store, and manage PDX-based experimental data generated by the projects; to facilitate exchange of PDX models between the PDXNet program; and to facilitate transfer of experimental data to the PDTC Bioinformatics Core and the PDTC PDXNet Data Commons and Coordinating Center to relate treatment responses to the molecular characteristics of individual patients’ tumors. Our PDTC PDX Core current comprises 262 breast PDX lines available for projects within our PDTC Center and across the PDXNet program.

title: Elucidating Biomolecular Dynamics using Magnetic Resonance Augmented by Machine Learning and Quantum Technologies
text:
Post-translational modifications employed by cells regulate fundamental biological processes such as cellular
signaling and offer promising avenues for therapeutic applications. This proposal provides a cutting-edge
approach to elucidate the macromolecular dynamics at the heart of these processes using novel magnetic
resonance paradigms leveraging machine learning, quantum computing, and nanoscale quantum sensing. The
innovative analysis and experimental methodologies presented here have the potential to illuminate
fundamental questions in biology and facilitate the development of novel therapeutics across a wide span of
illnesses.

title: The role of placental macrophages in cytomegalovirus infection at the maternal-fetal interface
text:
Human Cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is the most common cause of congenital infection, leading to hearing loss and
various developmental disabilities in affected newborns, with the potential for life-long consequences. Despite its
substantial clinical and economic impact, our understanding of how HCMV crosses the placenta to infect the
fetus remains incomplete, and the specific role of placental macrophages in managing or permitting HCMV
transmission is especially obscure. This research will contribute fundamental knowledge about the mechanism
and functional impact of HCMV infection in placental macrophages; vital in our efforts to develop preventative
and therapeutic strategies against congenital HCMV.
